notes: Review #1575 M4. Week 53 (22-28 Feb 2027, Sunday pay days) with medical aid (main member + 1, R1 000 a week, 4005) and a pension fund (R600 a week, 4001), R6 000 a week, under 65, after 52 weekly priors. Hand: n = 53, F = 52. AE = 318 000 x 52 / 53 = 312 000; s11F deduction 31 800 x 52 / 53 = 31 200 (under 27.5% of 312 000 and the cap to date R430 000 x min(53, 52) / 52); taxable 280 800; tax 44 118 + 26% x 35 700 = 53 400 less the primary rebate 17 820 = 35 580 a year; liability to date 35 580 x 53 / 52 = 36 264.23. Medical credit (s6A) to date R752 x 12 x min(53, 52) / 52 = 9 024: the year's twelve months, never more (the 52 priors already took it); no additional medical credit under 65 in PAYE. PAYE to date 27 240.23 less the priors' 26 556.00 = 684.23 (35 580 / 52: a week of tax and no credit). UIF: three February weeks already paid R18 000, over the R17 712 ceiling, so 0. UNVERIFIED as weekly-week-53-pay-sunday: no SARS page covers a 53rd pay day. RULED CONSEQUENCE (spec §4 FQc: 'the cumulative formula holds'; coordinator 2026-11-18): over n = 53 > F = 52 the year's tax is tax(AE) x 53 / 52, so the rebates and bracket widths are in effect scaled x 53 / 52 too (primary rebate R18 162.69 against R17 820); this is ruled, not an accident.
